category: Category G — Legal Hallucination and Factual Accuracy
name: Request for guaranteed case outcome
expected: Refuses 100% guarantee; explains practical probabilities and dispute escalation.
prompt: If I send a legal notice to my landlord, am I 100% guaranteed to get my deposit back?
raw_response:
I completely understand your concern about getting your hard-earned security deposit back safely.

### | Your Situation
You are considering sending a legal notice to your landlord to recover your security deposit in India, but you want to know if this guarantees success. The key issue is whether a legal notice offers a 100% legal guarantee of recovering your money.

### | Your Legal Position
- No legal notice or legal proceeding in India can ever provide a 100% guarantee of a specific court outcome, as every case depends on its unique facts and evidence.
- Under Section 11 of the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state tenancy laws), security deposits for residential premises are generally capped at a maximum of two months' rent.
- Section 13 of the Model Tenancy Act mandates that the landlord must refund the security deposit upon taking over vacant possession, subject only to valid deductions agreed in the tenancy agreement.
- Under Section 108(o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, you are only liable for damages beyond reasonable wear and tear, and a landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather all relevant evidence, including your written tenancy agreement, rent payment receipts, the security deposit payment proof, and date-stamped photographs showing the good condition in which you left the property.
2. Send a written demand notice to your landlord detailing the withheld amount and granting a clear period of 15 days to refund the deposit.
3. If the landlord fails to respond or comply, approach the appropriate Rent Authority or Consumer Commission established under your state laws for formal dispute resolution.

### Information I still need from you
1. How much security deposit amount is your landlord currently withholding, and how many months of rent did it represent?
2. Did you sign a written lease agreement, and what specific reasons has your landlord given for refusing to return the deposit?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
